**The CLJS ADAPTER PUBLICATION PINS for late-bind hooks are graded by the NODE lane ALONE, so a green browser lane beside green JVM artefacts is not evidence about THOSE PINS (rf2-uwa9r) — a claim about those pins and NOT about late-bind changes at large, because the JVM lane grades hook publication too (rf2-d3l8g; that half is at the end of this paragraph, and stopping at this sentence is how the old wording failed OPEN).** The publication cross-check is `reagent-slim-adapter-hooks-cross-checked-against-directory` in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_late_bind_publication_cljs_test.cljs`, which asserts the adapter's pinned hook set `=` the producer entries the authoritative directory (`re-frame.late-bind.directory/hooks`) lists for it. Its namespace ends `-cljs-test`, and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`'s `:browser-test` build selects `.*-dom-cljs-test$` — so the browser lane never loads it — while `:node-test` selects `cljs-test$`, which does; and it is a `.cljs` file, so no JVM artefact compiles it. **That holds for the whole CLJS class rather than one file**: all four `*late_bind*_cljs_test.cljs` namespaces end `-cljs-test` and none ends `-dom-cljs-test`, against a live control of 212 `-dom-cljs-test` files in the tree. **So when you change an adapter's published hook set, run `npm run test:cljs`.** Measured on PR #9904: a green browser lane at 1111 tests / 6083 assertions / 0 failures AND 21 of 21 JVM artefacts green, with that assertion failing between them — two clean columns and a live red in the gap. This is the rf2-p0b0 two-zeros-sharing-one-blind-spot shape in the paragraph above reached through a NEW DOOR: there the corroborating instruments were two searches, here they are two green gate lanes, routed by NAMESPACE SUFFIX rather than by search pattern. **THE JVM HALF, WHICH THE EARLIER WORDING DENIED: this paragraph once opened "a change that adds, removes or renames a LATE-BIND HOOK is graded by the NODE lane ALONE", and that universal is FALSE and fails OPEN (rf2-d3l8g)** — it tells a worker who renames a hook that the JVM artefacts cannot catch it, so a green node lane reads as sufficient. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj` is a JVM `.clj` test pinning the authoritative directory against the in-tree `set-fn!`, `route-hook!`, `chain-fn!` and `set-fns!` publication sites in BOTH directions — `every-published-key-has-a-directory-entry` and `every-directory-entry-is-actually-published` among its eight `deftest`s — so an added, removed or renamed hook IS graded there; and the per-artefact `late_bind_missing_test.clj` files flip hooks to pin the artefact-missing contract, one of them (`dormant-routing-late-bind-hooks-are-unpublished-rf2-sy7zr`) pinning a REMOVAL outright. Measured 2026-09-17: of the 12 tracked `*late_bind*` test files **8 are JVM `.clj` against 4 CLJS**, so the census behind the false universal had counted only the CLJS third of the class — the pattern-pre-decides-its-answer shape the paragraph above names, one door on. **So the node lane is NECESSARY for the CLJS pins and NOT SUFFICIENT for a hook change: run `npm run test:cljs` AND the JVM artefact sweep (`scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`, whose roster includes `implementation/core`).** **The lanes are correct and this wants no new gate** — what was missing was the map.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (link-validation-gates), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

**Link validation is split across two gates, and the split does not follow the job name.** `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates markdown link targets and heading anchors under `docs/`, `spec/`, `skills/`, `migration/` and `tools/*/spec` — and **nothing else**: repo-root markdown (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `TESTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`) and every `README.md` beside source code, `implementation/**` included, are outside its roots, where it **exits 0 on a broken link**. Those are `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`'s surface, which models GitHub's `-N` duplicate-heading suffix where the docs gate models MkDocs' `_N`. **That division is by ROOT, never by filename: a `README.md` at ANY depth under `docs/`, `spec/`, `migration/` or `skills/` is the DOCS gate's, so "every `README.md` beside source code" above means outside those four roots** — `check_readme_links.py`'s `DOCS_GATE_ROOTS` test walks `rel.parents`, so `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/README.md` is excluded from it exactly as `skills/README.md` is, and **8** of those READMEs do sit beside source code. Measured at `40b9e07f19`: of the **38** `README.md` files under those four roots the README gate walks **0** and the docs gate **37** — the 38th sits under a `findings/` directory, excluded below — against a control the other way, `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md`, which is the README gate's. **An absolute `http(s)` URL is skipped by both gates as CI runs them UNLESS a gate unwraps it to a repo path, and the shapes unwrapped today are this repository's own `https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/(blob|tree)/main/<path>[#anchor]` URL** — the spelling a shipped skill doc must use to cite outside its package (rf2-nvbz) — which `check_doc_slugs.py` grades against the working tree: existence (any target kind), `blob/` for a file and `tree/` for a directory, and on a `.md` blob the anchor GitHub renders (`_in_repo_github_url_problems`; `main` only, so a sha- or tag-pinned URL stays skipped) — and, since rf2-dnx3r, this project's own `https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/<path>[#anchor]` site URLs, in BOTH gates: the path resolved offline to the page or asset MkDocs would publish there, and an anchor on a page graded against the headings MkDocs renders on it (`_site_url_link_problems`, one helper both gates call, so the README gate grades it by MkDocs' `_N` duplicate suffix rather than its own GitHub `-N`). `check_readme_links.py --ci` has no GitHub arm, so a GitHub cite in root markdown or a README beside source is verified by hand — say so in the PR body (rf2-3pwdo). Since rf2-i4nb2 that surface is **three** rosters rather than two — git-tracked non-`README.md` markdown beside source is the third (`implementation/SECURITY.md`, `examples/TESTING.md` and a handful more that no gate reached before), narrow by design, with `scripts/_test_fixtures/`, the docs-gate roots and `tools/*/spec/` all still excluded. **And the docs gate's roots are narrower than its list reads: `check_doc_slugs.py` skips every directory named `findings` wherever it sits (`EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES`, deliberately, as exploratory work), and because `check_readme_links.py --ci` excludes all of `tools/*/spec/` while `mkdocs_hooks.py` stages no `tools/` tree, the committed findings corpora — `tools/story/spec/findings/**` and `tools/xray/spec/findings/**` — are validated by NO link gate, so check their links by hand and say so** (rf2-sdn0l, measured on one tree: a broken anchor planted in `tools/story/spec/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/matrix.md` left both gates at exit 0, while the same anchor in `tools/story/spec/023-Parity-Test.md` turned `check_doc_slugs.py` red naming file and line). **Both run in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job on every PR** — that job carries no surface guard, which is what rf2-v7fui secured for the docs gate — so the surface is gated, and the repair for a wrong nomination is to name the right gate, never to add one. Both also run in the fast-PR spine, but there they sit inside its **documentation tier, which is classifier-gated**: a green spine on a diff the classifier did not call documentation ran neither of them, so cite CI for these two rather than a local spine pass. But **that job's NAME reads as though it checks READMEs while the gate that actually does is the other one**, so nominate by PATH, never by job name: a broken target planted in `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` returns `check_doc_slugs.py` green and `check_readme_links.py --ci` red (rf2-8pb5k, measured twice). **And `mkdocs build --strict` does not validate heading ANCHORS at all — not even on a page it builds and publishes, so `exclude_docs` and `docs_dir` do not exhaust its non-coverage**: MkDocs grades a missing anchor, in-page or cross-file, at INFO (`validation.anchors` defaults to `info`, and `mkdocs.yml` sets no `anchors` key — only `links.unrecognized_links`), and `--strict` promotes WARNING but not INFO, so the strict build names the broken anchor on stdout and still exits 0. That leaves `check_doc_slugs.py` the only anchor gate for pages under `docs/` — **redundancy missing rather than coverage missing**, since it runs unguarded on every PR (rf2-zk50, measured on one planted anchor: docs gate exit 1 naming file, line and anchor; strict build exit 0). **So for the staged trees the two gates are COMPLEMENTARY rather than redundant, and neither substitutes for the other: `check_doc_slugs.py` validates ANCHORS and REPO-RELATIVE targets — what GitHub browsing needs — while `mkdocs build --strict` validates LINK RESOLUTION INSIDE THE BUILT SITE, which the slug gate cannot see at all.** A link can be correct on one and broken on the other, and a page under `spec/` is where that bites, because staging moves it: `mkdocs_hooks.py` rewrites the depth-1 form `](../docs/` to `](../` (`_SPEC_TO_DOCSROOT`), but there is **no depth-2 analogue, no `docs/` entry in the `_REWRITES` GitHub-URL fallback table, and no depth dispatch in the `spec/` branch** the way the guide branch dispatches on source depth — so a page in a `spec/` SUBDIRECTORY cannot reach `docs/` by a relative path at all, while a page at the top of `spec/` reaches it fine (453 such `](../docs/` links across 28 files are live and resolve in the built site). Measured on one tree with a single planted link in `spec/conformance/README.md`: `mkdocs build --strict` exit 1 naming the file and the unresolvable target, `check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0 and silent on the same tree (rf2-3r2t). `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under `docs/design/fresco/` as its own `docs.yml` job. **And neither gate looks inside a fenced code block at all**, which bounds every green above a second time and along a different axis than the rosters: both share one extractor, and it strips fences before it reads a single link, so a broken target or anchor written inside a fence is invisible and the exit 0 is silent about it (rf2-sodfq, measured in both directions — the identical broken anchor returns exit 0 inside a fence and exit 1 four lines above it in prose). The skip is deliberate and stays: well over a hundred in-repo doc links live inside fences, most of them in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` as `;;` commentary inside schema samples, and a fence is code — this repo's own write-ups quote broken links on purpose. Only `docs/design/fresco/` and `docs/the-mayor-method/` are held to more, and there the rule is the opposite one: a doc link inside a fence is itself reported, because those trees' fences are pasteable deliverables. **So for an edit CONFINED to a fenced block — and whole pages qualify, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`'s schemas among them — neither gate is the gate**: nominating one returns a green that inspected nothing you changed, so check the links by hand and say so. **That reasoning is not about FENCES — it holds wherever the file contains none of what the gate inspects, and the commonest case is a page with NO LINKS AT ALL, where a link gate cannot fail and its green is indistinguishable from a real pass.** Measured 2026-09-17 with the gate's own extractor, **20 of the 488** tracked `.md` pages under `docs/`, `spec/` and `migration/` carry zero links — `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` among them, at 0 links and 0 fences — against a both-ways control of 468 pages carrying 16,069 links between them; and `check_doc_slugs.py`'s per-file loop runs entirely off the links it extracts, so its one link-INDEPENDENT check (the `HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS` manifest, which genuinely does red on an anchor nothing links to) rescues nothing here, covering 12 enumerated pages and **none of the 20**. **So before nominating a gate, check the file CONTAINS what that gate inspects; where it does not, say so and verify by hand** (rf2-9h0f9). Nothing validates any of this markdown's PROSE, tables, rendering or nav — link targets and anchors are the whole of what these gates check — so **the worker verifies anchors and table column counts by hand and says so in the PR body**.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (merge-criterion-traps), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

- **Three mechanical traps in the merge criterion are recorded here rather than left to the method doc, because each fails OPEN — each ADMITS a merge that should have been blocked, and each is one small step from correct.** The criterion itself is not restated here; it is [`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md`](docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md#1-merge) §1, clauses 1–5. **(a) The job-key discriminator needs TWO LEADING SPACES**: `git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'`. Job keys nest under `jobs:`, so the unindented form matches nothing at all — it read 0 across the last twenty `.github/workflows/` commits, including all five that genuinely added a job, and a constant zero is the reassuring answer, so nothing on screen betrays it. Exercised in both directions rather than only where the answer is zero: the two-space form reads `1` on `366e4fca79`, which added a job, and `0` on `4cf4d711a2`, which added none; the unindented form reads `0` on both. **But a NON-ZERO count is a question rather than an answer, and that follow-up runs the OTHER way — it fails CLOSED, flagging a merge that should proceed, which is why it is a qualification to (a) and not a fourth trap. A zero is still the reassuring answer this paragraph warns about; nothing here narrows that.** The discriminator counts job keys across EVERY file under `.github/workflows/`, but clause 5 is about the checks a PULL REQUEST is graded on, and a workflow with no `pull_request` trigger contributes none — measured 2026-09-05, 7 of the 11 workflow files here carried no `pull_request` trigger at all, so most of the directory the discriminator reads can never move a rollup. Measured on PR #9277: merge-base `b86310b3c1` → `origin/main` read `wf=271 jobkeys=1`, the single key was `mcp-live-windows` added to `.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml`, whose `on:` is `schedule` plus `workflow_dispatch` and no `pull_request`; the band did not move, and #9277's own rollup came in at the same 87 as the four PRs merged before it. Discharge the flag with the file name the same diff already carries on its `+++ b/<path>` lines — `git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -E '^(\+\+\+|\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$)'` — then read the `on:` block of each named file and count only keys in files carrying a `pull_request` trigger. **AND THAT DISCHARGE ASKS WHETHER THE *FILE* CARRIES A `pull_request` TRIGGER, NEVER WHETHER THE *MATCHED LINE* WAS A JOB KEY — so confirm each matched key sits under `jobs:` rather than under `on:`.** A workflow's `on:` block puts `push:`, `pull_request:` and `workflow_dispatch:` at that same two-space indent, so the discriminator matches those too: measured 2026-09-17 at `03b51187e4` over whole files — the upper bound rather than the everyday error, the discriminator running against a diff of ADDED lines — all eleven workflow files over-count, 140 matched keys against 119 real jobs. **It can only INFLATE, so the reassuring zero above is untouched and this is NO fourth fail-open trap**: it fails CLOSED exactly as the rename mirror below does and carries the same phantom-band cost, but it arrives THROUGH the discharge, because on a diff that ADDS a trigger the question *does this file carry a `pull_request` trigger?* is answered yes by the very line that caused the false positive. **Operational rather than theoretical**: of the 423 commits touching `.github/workflows/`, 16 add `on:`-block keys, and `b853f9d57db5` is the pure case — the discriminator reads 1, the mirrored pattern reads 0 removals so the rename check below does not catch it either, the named `docs.yml` does carry a `pull_request` trigger, and the truth is ZERO jobs added, the matched line BEING the trigger that commit was adding; `a9a7a151337c` reads 6 against 2 real jobs. **Take the tell from the STRUCTURE rather than from the trigger vocabulary — a job key's block carries `runs-on:`, and a trigger's never does** (or `uses:`, which a reusable-workflow call job carries INSTEAD of `runs-on:`; nothing in this tree is one today, so that half is unexercised here). Measured that day, 119 of 119 jobs carry `runs-on:` while none of the 21 `on:` keys carries either. A list of trigger NAMES is the tempting alternative and the worse one: it goes stale as GitHub adds events, and it DEFLATES — the dangerous direction — against a job legitimately named `release` or `schedule`. Both ways on trap (a)'s own cited commit, `366e4fca79`'s single matched key sits under `jobs:` carrying `runs-on:`, so the correction still reads it as the real new check it is. **AND ONE INFERENCE PAST THAT CORRECTION IS THE FAIL-OPEN DOOR — IT IS THE DISCHARGE AND NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR: THE STRUCTURAL CHECK COUNTS JOB DEFINITIONS, WHILE CLAUSE 5 ASKS WHETHER THE CHECK SET WAS COMPUTED AGAINST THE MATRIX ON THE TRUNK NOW, AND ZERO JOB DEFINITIONS ADDED IS COMPATIBLE WITH EXISTING JOBS NEWLY PARTICIPATING IN PR CHECKS.** Everything above stands exactly as written — the over-count really can only INFLATE and the reassuring zero really is untouched — because none of it is about the check SET. A workflow's `on:` block decides which of its jobs a pull request schedules, and that can move while the jobs themselves do not, so discounting a matched key as a trigger discharges the JOB-COUNT flag and discharges nothing whatever about clause 5. [`loops.md`](docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md#1-merge) says it for the clause as a whole — *clause 5 is reading, not counting*, and the band is measured on changes merged after the last MATRIX change — and a trigger-only commit is a matrix change carrying no job key at all. **So when the matched keys turn out to be `on:`-block keys, that is the flag REPOINTED rather than cleared: ask what the new block schedules that the old one did not.** **The pure case above is the demonstration, and its record here stopped one sentence short.** Re-measured at `cc1b78078f`: `b853f9d57db5` adds `pull_request` (carrying `branches: [main]` and a five-entry `paths:` list) beside the existing push and workflow_dispatch, leaves `build` and `deploy` exactly as they were — both carrying `runs-on:` either side — and newly gates `deploy` with `if: github.event_name == 'push'`; its own subject says PRs should surface build regressions before merge. Job-definition delta **zero**, effective check-set delta **+2**, and the historical band settles that rather than the YAML alone: `spec/`-only PR #238, whose merge commit does NOT carry `b853f9d57db5` as an ancestor, read a settled rollup of **18** with **no** `docs` rows, while `spec/`-only PR #245, whose merge commit does, read **20** with **two** — `MkDocs build` SUCCESS and `Deploy to GitHub Pages` SKIPPED. Controls both ways: `tests` contributed 18 on each side, and exactly ONE commit touching `.github/workflows/` sits between the two merge commits — that one — against 7 commits in the range. **A job gated OFF by `if:` still contributes a band row**, since clause 2 accepts skipped, so push-gating `deploy` never removed it: `Deploy to GitHub Pages` read `COMPLETED` / `SKIPPED` on #245 and reads it again today. **The fail-open direction is a band left stale LOW** — keep the old band across an added trigger and a rollup GENUINELY missing those same rows reads as at-band and merges, which is clause 1's failure admitted through clause 5. The mirror, a trigger removed or a `paths:` list narrowed, fails closed into the phantom band priced above, and loops.md's *read which key left* remedy cannot reach it, because no key left. **The repair needs no new mechanism: it is the rollup TOTAL of a PR merged after the suspect commit, already prescribed above — BUT TAKE IT ON A PR WHOSE FILES MATCH THE TRIGGER'S `paths:` LIST, or the confirmation hands back the PRE-CHANGE number and corroborates the wrong answer.** Measured both ways against one post-trigger matrix eleven minutes apart: #242, three of its seven files matching, read **20**; #243, whose single file matched none of the list, read **18** — the pre-trigger number exactly. So a path-filtered workflow contributes a different count to different PRs, and while it stays filtered there is no single band for it. **Do not reason today's `docs.yml` back onto that date**: its PR trigger is now deliberately UNFILTERED with the docs surface re-applied job-side by a `detect` job, and its six jobs contribute six of the 88 rows on PR #9984, a settled rollup whose only changed file was `CLAUDE.md`. **An events roster remains the wrong answer** for the reason already given; what changes is only which question you ask of the block. **This is no licence to discount `test.yml`**, whose `pull_request` trigger is deliberately unfiltered — its `paths-ignore` list sits under `push:` alone — so a key added there is a real new check **UNLESS THE SAME DIFF REMOVES ONE: the discriminator inspects `+` lines only, so a RENAMED job reads as a pure addition and fakes a band move.** Count removals with the mirrored pattern before concluding anything — `git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^-  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'` — and read added == removed with pairwise-corresponding names as a RENAME, which moves the band by zero. Measured 2026-09-10 at trunk `d9ba7e8ac2`: a 24-hour window of workflow churn read **7 added keys, 5 of them in `test.yml`**, which by the discharge above is "five real new checks" and a band of 92 — while the mirrored pattern read **7 removed** over that same diff, every one the pre-rename twin of an added name (all of it `8b17cc53d5`, a product-name sweep), and the band read **87 before and 87 after**: #9564–#9567 merged before that commit and #9626–#9629 after it, all eight at 87 with nothing non-terminal. **The cheaper confirmation needs no pattern at all — read the rollup TOTAL of a PR merged AFTER the suspect commit**, and four PRs at 87 across a commit that "added five jobs" settles it in one query. This fails CLOSED like the qualification above, but the cost is real: it invents a band that never existed, after which every PR reads five checks short of a phantom — indistinguishable from a change genuinely missing five jobs, and the next move is to hunt for coverage that was never gone. Rename sweeps are routine here, with a live gate ratcheting the retired product name out of the tree, so this recurs. **(b) Pass the FULL 40-character head oid to `gh run list --commit`, taken from `gh pr view --json headRefOid` — never extended by hand from an abbreviated sha.** An abbreviated sha matches nothing, returns `[]`, and clears the live-runs check vacuously — and a hand-fabricated full-length sha returns the same `[]` while satisfying the full-40-characters rule in form (measured 2026-09-01: PR #8829 read a full 84-check rollup beside `[]` from a sha extended from a report's 10-char prefix; the re-queried oid returned 4 completed runs). A full rollup beside an empty run list is the tell — re-query, don't conclude. Clause 4 states the trap generically under *Abbreviated revisions*; what is here is the CLI concretion it does not name. **(c) `All required checks passed` is a REAL JOB — never subtract it from the band, and never merge on it alone. AND IT IS NOT THE ONLY ROW OF ITS KIND, so the reflex below costs one from the band for EACH such row discounted rather than one in total.** It is `test.yml`'s `all-required-passed` aggregator (`if: ${{ always() }}`, `needs:` every gating job in that file), and it presents in the rollup as an ordinary three-second CheckRun in workflow `tests`, which is exactly what invites the misreading: it reads like a host-generated "everything is green" summary row, so the reflex is to discount it and derive a band one LOWER — after which a rollup genuinely one job short reads as at-band and merges. **Other `pull_request` workflows carry their own, so the reader who spots the pattern discounts them all and derives a band several lower — the identical failure with more room in it. ENUMERATE them off the workflow FILES rather than trusting any tally, this file's included: an aggregator is a job key whose block carries `if: ${{ always() }}` and whose `needs:` lists other jobs in its OWN file.** Read that from the YAML and never from the rollup's display names — a substring match on a name points at the wrong job while looking perfectly clean, which is how this defect was nearly mis-sited when it was found. **Both tempting universals are false against this tree: it is not ONE, and it is not one PER WORKFLOW either, because `portability.yml` has none** — which is why the signature is recorded here and the count deliberately is not, a count being stale the moment portability gains one. Whatever the enumeration returns, the rule does not move: **never subtract ANY of them, and never merge on ANY of them alone.** **It fails open in the opposite direction too, and that reading is the more tempting one**: GitHub's `needs:` cannot span workflow files, so each aggregator covers its OWN workflow's jobs and no others — `test.yml`'s reaches `test.yml` alone, while `lint`, `docs` and `portability` run as separate workflows outside its reach. **That they sit outside it is NOT to say they have none of their own**, and the ones that do are evidence about their own workflow and nothing wider — so a green aggregator is not a green rollup, several green aggregators are not one either, and the five clauses still apply to the whole set. Measured 2026-09-01 across five PRs at once, when the band was in the low eighties: totals of 82, 83 and 84 all occurred, the aggregator was PRESENT on a PR still carrying two non-terminal checks (#8857, total 82) and ABSENT on two still building their sets (#8855 and #8856, total 83) — so its presence tracks neither the total nor settledness, and **a raw count is not comparable across PRs mid-build**. **Those totals are a dated illustration, never the band**: the band moves as jobs land, so it is re-measured at the top of every merge tick from the PRs actually in front of you, and no figure quoted in this file is the thing to compare a rollup against. Its own pass rule mirrors clause 2 (`needs.*.result`: `success` and `skipped` accepted, `failure` and `cancelled` refused), and `test.yml` deliberately keeps its `pull_request` trigger UNFILTERED so the aggregator is always scheduled — a path-filtered trigger would make it absent on filtered PRs, which is the phantom-pending trap rf2-dtvmb fixed.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (mkdocs-coverage), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

Docs build from repo root with `mkdocs build --strict` (config in `mkdocs.yml`). **Where the bare `mkdocs` console script is not on PATH — measured here exiting 127, which a pipeline reads as a failed build rather than a missing tool — invoke it as `python -m mkdocs build --strict` (mkdocs 1.6.1 answers that form on this box). Every nomination of `mkdocs build --strict` in this file means EITHER form; do not read a 127 as the docs being broken, and check the entry point before spending a run on it.**

**`mkdocs build --strict` does not cover `docs/design/**`** — `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` block deliberately keeps the design trees out of the site (they are working design records, not user-facing documentation), so never nominate it as the gate for an edit confined to that tree. **That block is the authority on what the build cannot see from WITHIN `docs_dir`, and it holds more than the design trees; read `exclude_docs` in `mkdocs.yml` before nominating `mkdocs build` for any path under `docs/`, rather than trusting a list in prose — a prose list drifts, and this one already had, naming two of the six trees the block excluded (rf2-yxuta).** But `exclude_docs` is only one of **two doors**, and the other is the one that catches people: `docs_dir` is `docs`, so anything outside it — `implementation/**`, `examples/**`, `tools/**`, `.github/**`, repo-root markdown — was never a candidate for exclusion and will never appear in that block (`mkdocs_hooks.py` classes `implementation/` as "CLJS source; not docs" and rewrites such references to GitHub URLs). **Absence from `exclude_docs` is therefore not evidence that the build covers a path**; check `docs_dir` first, or the wrong-gate nomination below simply recurs through the other door (rf2-8pb5k).

**But `docs_dir` does not bound the build's reach either, and the third door runs the OTHER way — INTO the build: `spec/` and `migration/` ARE covered by the strict build, because `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s `on_pre_build` hook stages them into `docs_dir` before MkDocs scans a single file** (its `_STAGE` table maps `spec` → `docs/spec` and `migration` → `docs/migration`; the staged copies are gitignored as `/docs/spec/` and `/docs/migration/`, so they never dirty a tree). **So `docs_dir: docs` is true but NOT dispositive, and reading it as "the strict build cannot see `spec/`" is the misreading that put a wrong gate nomination in roughly a dozen briefs (rf2-3r2t).** **The staging lives in the HOOK, not only in CI, so it runs on ANY invocation — `build`, `serve`, `--strict`, local or CI — and a BARE local `mkdocs build --strict` covers `spec/` with no manual staging step of your own.** That hook landed 2026-05-19 (`b2e622c316`, rf2-qw5mh) and its own comment says it exists so that any local or CI invocation auto-stages; `.github/workflows/docs.yml` keeps an explicit `rm -rf docs/spec && cp -r spec docs/spec` step that the file itself calls redundant belt-and-braces. **Do not tell a worker to replicate the staging by hand, and do not discount a local strict run as not covering `spec/` — both were measured wrong.** Measured on one tree by deleting `docs/spec` and `docs/migration` outright and running a bare `mkdocs build --strict`: both directories were recreated by the hook and 52 `spec/` pages were built, `spec/conformance/README.md` among them.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (reader-conditional-lane-coverage), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

**A change confined to a `#?(:cljs …)` READER-CONDITIONAL branch is COMPILED by the CLJS lane ALONE — a JVM lane READS that branch but never compiles it — so a green JVM sweep is not evidence about the changed forms, and it fails OPEN on nearly every defect anybody ships (rf2-z0pma; found at its own cost by rf2-kk986, PR #9976).** The reader must read the unselected branch to find where it ends and discards only its VALUE, so the boundary is READ-time versus COMPILE-time rather than `:clj` versus `:cljs`: a fault that breaks READING — an unterminated string, an unbalanced delimiter, `:::x`, `1abc` — goes red on any JVM artefact whose classpath carries the file, while a fault that reads as well-formed data — a malformed `defn`, an unresolved var, a wrong arity, an odd `let` binding vector, a reference left dangling by a deletion — is silently green. Measured 2026-09-18 with `clojure.core/read` at `{:read-cond :allow :features #{:clj}}` over eight fixtures with controls both ways (memory `a-cljs-reader-conditional-branch-is-invisible-to-every-jvm-lane`), and again 2026-09-21 with `load-file` on Clojure 1.12.4: four such plants inside a `:cljs` branch all loaded OK, and the identical `defn` text moved into a `:clj` branch failed at macroexpansion — the plant is a real fault, and the blindness is the branch's. Both directions happened here within one day: rf2-kk986's first push was the green case — an EVEN number of stray quotes in a docstring, leaving `(defn f "doc " leaked " tail" [x] …)`, which lexes — and the CLJS compiler refused the namespace while 2313 core JVM tests, the 21-artefact sweep and all 46 ratchets read green; rf2-ic8lz's plant (PR #9998) was the red case — ONE stray quote at `config.cljc:900` took the tools/xray JVM suite to exit 1, `Invalid token`. **The surface is 149 of the 963 tracked `.cljc` files** (those carrying `#?(:cljs`; control `#?(:zzz` 0; re-measure). **THE TRAP, WORSE THAN THE FINDING: THE OBVIOUS POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES WHILE THE BLINDNESS STANDS.** A worker plants a syntax error in the branch, watches the JVM lane go red, and concludes the lane grades the branch — it saw a READ error, and is as blind as before to everything that compiles. So the positive control is a plant that READS as data and fails at MACROEXPANSION, shown GREEN on the JVM, and rf2-kk986's own fault is the measured one: `(defn probe-fn "doc " leaked " tail" [] nil)` inside the `:cljs` branch is green on the JVM (`load-file`, measured), green on clj-kondo (0 errors, 0 warnings, measured) and refused by the CLJS compiler (measured, rf2-kk986). **Do not reach for an unresolved var or a wrong arity as the CLJS-red half**: the CLJS compiler grades both as WARNINGS, no test build in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` sets `:warnings-as-errors` (0 matches; its own comment says `:browser-test` exits 0 on warnings), so the build stays green and the fault surfaces at runtime only if the path executes — a plant red nowhere proves nothing. **And clj-kondo is NOT the JVM lane and is NOT blind to the branch, so never cite it as though it were**: with this repo's `.clj-kondo/config.edn` (no `:cljc :features` key, so both dialects are linted) an unresolved symbol inside `#?(:cljs …)` warns exactly as inside `#?(:clj …)` (exit 2 both), and a wrong arity or an odd `let` errors at exit 3 — while the malformed-`defn` shape reads 0/0 in a `:cljs` branch, in a `:clj` branch AND outside any conditional. The byte-identical counts rf2-kk986 saw were a fact about clj-kondo's LINTERS, not about the reader conditional; read it as item (w) says, by finding lines and count delta, as supplementary evidence and never as a substitute for the compile. **THE GUARD, and no new gate**: for any `.cljc` change, say which branch the changed forms sit in; if `:cljs`, nominate `npm run test:cljs` (or the shadow build that includes the namespace) or state plainly that you rely on CI — a JVM green is not evidence about them and must be declared as such. Same class as the paragraph above through a NEW DOOR — there the routing is by NAMESPACE SUFFIX across files, here by READER CONDITIONAL inside one file — and deliberately not folded into it.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (shadow-cljs-build-lane), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

- **The shadow-cljs BUILD LANE — every shadow-cljs invocation, node and browser alike — is a MACHINE-WIDE EXCLUSIVE, and two concurrent runs WEDGE SILENTLY — no error, no exit file, no output, just two builds that never finish.** So the failure does not present as contention; it presents to each worker as a hang on its own gate, and to the coordinator as two unrelated "infrastructure" reports with nothing connecting them. **WHAT COUNTS AS ONE is the half the old label got wrong**: it read "the shadow-cljs / browser lane", and that slash reads as an apposition naming the browser lane alone — a real and NARROWER thing in this repo, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`'s `:browser-test` build, which is the sense the late-bind bullet below uses. So `npm run test:cljs` takes the lane exactly as `test:browser` does, and a brief nominating the node lane as a worker's gate while forbidding shadow-cljs builds in the next paragraph cannot be satisfied — issued in precisely that shape on 2026-09-17 with the lane already granted elsewhere, and a near-miss only because the worker measured the collision and asked instead of acting. **SO DO NOT TRUST A ROSTER OF SCRIPT NAMES — ASK `implementation/package.json`'s scripts block, and ask it what a script EXECUTES rather than what it MENTIONS.** Measured at `34390c784f`: of its 38 scripts, **34 reach shadow-cljs** and 4 do not (`test:fresco-invariants`, `test:fresco-lint`, `test:scripts`, `test:ssr-node` — two Python static checks, a `node --test` run whose only runner-mentioning files read source or stub it, and a lane that reads `shadow-cljs.edn` as text to assert absence). **A search for the literal `shadow-cljs` finds 10 of those 34**; adding `compile-node-test.cjs` gets 6 more and the dotted `shadow.cljs.devtools.cli` 1, which is the 17 a careful earlier sweep reported — **exactly half, and short in the direction that authorises a concurrent run.** The other 17 reach it through further `.cjs` wrappers that resolve `shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js` and spawn it under `process.execPath` — `check-examples-compile.cjs`, `dev-testbed.cjs`, `story-build.cjs`, `serve-example.cjs`, `check_modules_compile.cjs` and the `serve-and-run-*.cjs` harnesses among them — and `test:story-static` reaches it at TWO hops, through `check-story-static.cjs` spawning `story-build.cjs`. **The reliable question is therefore not "does the command say shadow-cljs" but "does anything it runs, at any depth, ENTER THE SHADOW-CLJS COMPILER/BUILD RUNTIME BY ANY ENTRY POINT"** — the Node runner `shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js` and the wrappers that resolve it, and EQUALLY a direct `shadow.cljs.devtools.cli` or `shadow.cljs.devtools.api` call on a JVM classpath carrying the `thheller/shadow-cljs` jar. A name-shaped search under-reports by construction, because it finds the wrappers its author already knew, which is how the 17 came to be half — **and a RUNNER-shaped one under-reports too, which is the same defect one level down and the one that bit this very paragraph**: phrased as "reaches `shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js`" it EXCLUDED the dotted CLI that the roster above it COUNTS, so the recipe contradicted its own inventory and failed OPEN, which is the direction that authorises a concurrent run. `test:tools-machines-viz` is the live instance and the whole class: `clojure -M:cljs-test -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile …`, with the jar pinned on `tools/machines-viz/deps.edn`'s `:cljs-test` alias, taking the lane exactly as `test:cljs` does while NO runner appears anywhere in its launch path — the CLI namespace resolves its own actual `-main`, whose `:compile` arm enters `api/compile*` and stays JVM-side throughout. **So ask what a command ENTERS, never which launcher it travels through**: a Node hop is one way in, not the definition, and the JVM is the other. **This is written down HERE because it was measured to have no tracked home at all (2026-09-16): `exclusive` reads 0 in this file and 0 in [`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md`](docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md); [`loops.md`](docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md) carries it 4 times and every one is the DISPATCH FILTER (do not send two items at one contended resource), not the take-and-release protocol; and the single tracked file matching shadow-cljs beside exclusive is a migration eval about mutually exclusive BUILD MODES. Control both ways over the same corpus: `hot-zone` reads 85 tracked files, a nonsense token 0.** So the protocol existed only in per-dispatch brief text, retyped every tick — which is exactly how the fence wording drifted, one level up. **ANNOUNCE-AND-TAKE IS NOT A LOCK, and every party obeying it perfectly is still not enough.** Measured the same day, a genuine near-miss: worker A announced RELEASING and promised to announce before re-taking; the mayor, on the strength of that, told worker B the lane was free; B announced TAKING; A then announced RE-TAKING exactly as promised. Nobody broke the rule and the lane was doubly held, because **an announcement NOTIFIES and does not ASK, so two correct announcements compose into a collision.** The rules, and the first three are the coordinator's rather than the worker's: **FIRST ACQUIRER HOLDS** — an announcement is not an acquisition when someone else is already in the window; **never grant on the strength of a release message alone**, because a release is evidence about the past, so check that nobody has announced a take since; **grant explicitly to ONE worker and keep a queue**, telling the next worker its place is held so it does not have to ask again, since an asking worker is a worker tempted to assume; and **a worker told to yield KILLS any run already started rather than letting it finish** — a half-overlapped run is as wedged as a fully overlapped one — verifying by EFFECT (identify your processes by ANCESTRY — note the PID of what you launched and walk its descendants through `ParentProcessId`, which is also what keeps a peer's out of reach; kill that tree children-first FROM POWERSHELL, since from Git Bash `taskkill /T` meets the `/FLAG` rewrite of instrument item (h) and `cmd /c` is the silent no-op the worktree-removal bullet records; then READ every `node.exe`/`java.exe` row with its parent chain — never a path filter, never a bare count) and deleting the partial log so nobody reads a half-written file as a verdict. **A worktree-path filter over command lines sees only a SUBSET of one build, so "zero remain" can read true while the build lives** (rf2-fvxg5, measured 2026-09-18 at `717bca7b5d`): of a node-lane build's three live compile processes only shadow-cljs's `runner.js` named its worktree, because npm launches the wrapper by a relative path and the JVM receives a relative `-cp`, and the run phase after them is a bare `node out/node-test.js` — while walking the parent chain attributed that JVM to its tree correctly; the coordinator's pre-grant census counts machine-wide with no path filter, so it fails CLOSED and is not to be narrowed into one. **Tell the yielding worker whose fault it was**: here it had followed the protocol exactly and had kept its idle window deliberately short, which is the good behaviour that opened the gap, and saying so plainly stops it reading a coordination failure as a mark against its own run. **A worker that overlapped, even briefly, says so** — the holder then RE-RUNS rather than debugging a result, which is much the cheaper failure mode, and re-takes any baseline captured in the window, since a contaminated baseline poisons every column measured against it. **The deeper shape, which generalises past this lane: a rule phrased as "announce X" tells you what to SAY and not what to CHECK. Where the cost of two holders is silent destruction, the protocol needs a step that can REFUSE, and only something that sees all holders can refuse — absent an arbiter, the exclusive is not exclusive.** **Prefer avoiding the shared tree entirely**: install `node_modules` from the lockfile in the worktree (`npm ci`) rather than junctioning the mayor's, since nothing to unlink beats unlinking correctly — and see the worktree-removal bullet above for why a junction is dangerous and how to verify the shared tree afterwards.

CLAUDE.md PASSAGE (worktree-removal), FULL TEXT. CLAUDE.md now carries a compressed form of this rule; this memory is the complete account, measurements included, exactly as it stood at trunk bba75d0f5b before rf2-bidyt trimmed the file. Surrounding context: git show bba75d0f5b:CLAUDE.md

- **Remove a worker worktree only via `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh`** (POSIX primary; `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/remove-worker-worktree.ps1` on Windows). **Hand it a PATH, never a bare worktree name**: targets resolve against your CURRENT DIRECTORY, so `remove-worker-worktree.sh xraygate-a` run from the mayor checkout names `<mayor-checkout>/xraygate-a`, which does not exist — pass the absolute path, i.e. the string `git worktree list` already prints, and a target that is not an existing directory is refused with `REFUSED_BAD_ARGUMENT=` and exit 2 before any tree is examined (rf2-u62e; the bare-name form previously refused *after* the canary block, so a `tail` of the run showed six `CANARY_AFTER=` lines and no explanation). A worker worktree junctions `implementation/node_modules` at the mayor checkout's real one, and a bare `git worktree remove` follows that junction and empties the mayor's real `node_modules` — exit 0, silently, breaking every local build until `npm ci --prefix implementation` restores it. It has happened twice. The script unlinks the link first, removes the worktree second, then re-checks the mayor's `node_modules` counts and fails loudly if any dropped. **A worker that creates the junction removes it as its last act before reporting done**, so hygiene never meets one. **And never reach for `cmd /c` to make or break a junction from Git Bash: it is a SILENT NO-OP THAT RETURNS EXIT 0.** It prints the Windows banner, drops into an interactive prompt and runs nothing — so every `cmd /c rmdir "<junction>"` cleanup line shipped in a brief reports success and removes nothing, leaving live exactly the junction the next recursive delete follows into. That is the hazard above reached through a different door. Measured on a scratch junction: from Git Bash `cmd /c mklink /J` exits 0 with NO link created and `cmd /c rmdir` exits 0 with the junction still present; the identical commands from PowerShell work (`Junction created`). Use PowerShell for both — `New-Item -ItemType Junction`, `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false)` — and **verify the EFFECT, not the exit code**: list the link after creating it, and after removing confirm the link is gone AND the target still counts what it did. `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` is UNAFFECTED and needs no change — it invokes `cmd` nowhere, detects a junction with `[ -L ]`, unlinks with a plain non-recursive `rm` (which under MSYS unlinks the link instead of following it), and snapshots the mayor's counts before and after.

A CLASSPATH-OVERLAY PLANT IS LOADED ONLY IF ITS ALIAS IS LISTED BEFORE :test — alias order on the clojure CLI decides classpath order, and a plant behind the real file is never loaded, so the sabotage run reads GREEN with nothing on screen saying why. Measured 2026-10-02 in implementation/schemas (rf2-hd8xi control): `clojure -Sdeps '{:aliases {:ov {:extra-paths [OV]}}}' -Spath -M:ov:test` printed OV first, then test, then src; the same overlay passed as `-M:test:ovrun` (to make :ovrun's :main-opts win, since the LAST alias's :main-opts win) put OV after test, and a fixture plant ran green (6 tests, 0 failures). Rerun as `-M:ov:test:ovrun` (paths in a FIRST alias, :main-opts in a LAST one), the same plant went red (1 failure, the pinned digest literal). Guard: before believing a plant's colour, print which file the runtime loaded — `(str (.getResource (clojure.lang.RT/baseLoader) "re_frame/x/y_test.clj"))` names the overlay dir or the worktree. Also worth knowing: on JVM, `-M:ov:test -n <ns>` with the quiet runner runs one namespace in about 8 seconds here, so a plant-per-bead control batch costs under a minute.

CLJ-KONDO ON A TEST FILE ALONE MISSES TYPE ERRORS THAT NEED THE CALLEE'S SOURCE, so a per-file "no new findings" lint of a test edit can be clean while CI's clj-kondo job (which lints `--lint tools/xray` and the rest, src and test together, `--fail-level error`) goes red. Measured 2026-10-02 on a tools/xray panels test edit: `(-> (g/layout {...}) :nodes :l1 first :shared-count)` linted clean as a single file by path (0 findings), and errored when linted beside its source: `clj-kondo --lint tools/xray/src/.../reactive_flow_graph.cljc tools/xray/test/.../reactive_flow_graph_cljs_test.cljc` gave `error: Expected: seqable collection, received: map.` exit 3, the same line CI reported. Binding the call result with `let` first cleared it (exit 0). Guard: lint touched test files TOGETHER with the src tree they call (`clj-kondo --lint <artefact>/src <artefact>/test`), read `errors:` on the summary line, and convert Windows backslash paths before grepping the output for touched files.

A mayor checkpoint push to main (one .beads/issues.jsonl commit, a fast-forward of origin/main) was refused once with 'GH006: Protected branch update failed ... (protected branch hook declined)'. Measured 2026-10-03 ~00:00 AUSEST. The 'main' ruleset (id 16120663, unchanged since 2026-05-24) requires 3 status checks, and repository role 5 bypasses it always (current_user_can_bypass: always). A fresh fetch showed origin had not moved (HEAD^ == origin/main), and an identical re-push 1 minute later succeeded, printing the bypass notice '3 of 3 required status checks are expected'. gh pr merge --delete-branch EXITS 1 in the mayor checkout whenever the merged branch is still checked out in a worker worktree: the local branch delete is refused, and the whole command reports failure although the merge succeeded. So the merge's exit code stops telling a failed merge from a successful one. This repo already has delete_branch_on_merge=true (gh api repos/day8/re-frame2 --jq .delete_branch_on_merge), so the server deletes the remote branch itself, and the client flag adds nothing. Measured 2026-10-03 on #10790 and #10792: merge=1, state MERGED, remote ref gone. How to apply: merge with `gh pr merge <n> --rebase` and NO --delete-branch, read that exit code, confirm `gh pr view <n> --json state` reads MERGED, and delete the local branch with `git branch -D` only after the worktree is reaped. loops.md section 1 already says to prefer server-side deletion over a client delete flag.

GitHub issues get a bead each, and the issue closes WHEN ITS PR MERGES. Mike, 2026-10-04: "There are GH issues, action them as beads, and when the PRs merge for them, close the GH issue". This supersedes his 2026-10-03 wording ("The background agent which does the bead, should close the original issue"), under which workers closed issues at ready, before merge. How to apply: file one bead per open issue with --external-ref gh-<N> and the issue URL in the description, cluster same-surface issues into one dispatch, and brief the worker to put "Fixes #<N>" on its own line in the PR body and NOT to close the issue or the bead itself. At merge the mayor closes the bead and confirms with gh issue view <N> --json state that GitHub's closing keyword closed the issue, running gh issue close <N> --comment naming the PR if it did not.

GIT BASH DATE IGNORES IANA ZONE NAMES (measured 2026-10-04 on this machine). Converting a GitHub UTC timestamp to local time with an IANA zone name silently returns UTC, labelled as GMT, at exit 0: `TZ=Australia/Sydney date -d "2026-10-04T11:15:00Z" "+%H:%M %Z"` printed `11:15 GMT`. Formatted with a hard-coded "AUSEST" suffix, that becomes a false local time, eleven hours off. It reached two bead close reasons that way (rf2-vb28l, rf2-mk8tt; corrected by appended notes). A POSIX zone string is wrong too, because it has no DST rule: `TZ=AEST-10` printed `21:15 AEST` in daylight-saving time. THE WORKING FORM is plain `date -d "<utc-iso>" "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"`, which uses the machine's own zone: it printed `22:15 AUSEST`, and %Z supplies the label. CONTROL: the label in the output must be AUSEST or AUEST, never GMT. Never hard-code the zone suffix. Related: merged-pr-audit-powershell-utc-comparison (the PowerShell side of the same class).

THE SESSION-WIDE SUBAGENT CAP COUNTS WORKERS' OWN HELPER AGENTS, SO A MAYOR DISPATCH CAN BE REFUSED WITH ONLY FIVE WORKERS LIVE. Measured 2026-10-09 01:41 AUSEST in the rf2-txsk5 epic: with five workers running, the Agent tool refused the sixth dispatch with "Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run 20 subagents at once. Do not retry." The workers' briefs (prompt v2) invite read-only analyst subagents, and one worker alone reported eight, so five or six workers can hold the whole cap of 20. The same cap is why several workers reported "the Agent tool refused (concurrency limit), worked solo".
WHAT TO DO: do not retry in the same tick. Keep the prepared worktree and packet, write no ledger row until the dispatch succeeds (no agentId exists yet), and dispatch on the next tick or when a worker reports. An unattached worktree at trunk with no agent is the mayor's own; it has no done report, so the reap rule leaves it alone.
HOW TO APPLY: when saturating to six workers whose briefs allow analyst subagents, expect the first refusals around the cap; a worker that gets refused falls back to solo work at lower throughput, which is acceptable. The cap is raised only by the operator (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS).

A SECOND git fetch INSIDE THE SAME MERGE-CHECK COMMAND REWRITES FETCH_HEAD, SO EVERY LATER LINE GRADES THE WRONG BRANCH - AND IT CAN FAIL IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION. Measured 2026-10-09 03:08 AUSEST on PR #11008 (rf2-txsk5.4): the mayor's merge check ran `git fetch origin worker/p4-xray-settings`, took MB from FETCH_HEAD, then fetched worker/p4-xray-static mid-command to compute file overlap. Every line after that second fetch read the OTHER branch through FETCH_HEAD: it reported ".beads paths 1" and "39 overlapping files" for a PR that carried 0 and 0. Re-measured with remote-tracking refs (origin/worker/<branch>) it was clean, and it merged.
WHY IT MATTERS: here the wrong branch was dirtier, so the error was alarming and got caught. Fetch a CLEAN branch second and a PR carrying .beads paths, attribution lines or out-of-fence files reads clean - the gate passes on someone else's diff.
THE GUARD: in a merge check never read FETCH_HEAD; fetch each worker branch with an explicit refspec (`git fetch origin refs/heads/worker/X:refs/remotes/origin/worker/X`, which does update the tracking ref - see fetch-origin-branch-leaves-tracking-ref-stale) and grade origin/worker/X by name, checking its tip equals the PR's headRefOid. Related: pull-abort-cannot-fast-forward-multiple-branches (FETCH_HEAD shared across concurrent processes).
